questions.q: You want to know what a typical sale is worth. Which filter should the average deal size report use?
options: All opportunities regardless of stage
Only Closed Lost opportunities
Closed Won opportunities in the period
Only opportunities created this week
questions.explain: Averaging across open and lost deals mixes in amounts that were never sold. Restrict to Closed Won.

questions.q: Which report type gives one row per stage change, so you can measure time in stage?
options: Opportunities with Products
Opportunity History
Opportunities with Contact Roles
Accounts
questions.explain: Opportunity History records changes over time and provides stage duration.

questions.q: Why might summing the opportunity Amount in an Opportunities with Products report overstate revenue?
options: Products always add a fixed markup
Amount is not a numeric field
The report type hides closed deals
The parent opportunity Amount repeats on each line item row, so it is counted once per line
questions.explain: Child-row report types repeat the parent's fields. Sum the line item's own total field instead.

questions.q: How can you calculate sales cycle length in a native report?
options: Only with an external BI tool
A row-level formula subtracting Created Date from Close Date on won deals, or the standard Age field for open deals
By counting the number of records
By grouping by Owner alone
questions.explain: Age reports days since creation, and a row-level date formula gives creation-to-close days for won deals.

questions.q: A stage in Opportunity History has a much longer average stage duration than the others. What does that suggest?
options: It is a likely bottleneck where deals stall
That stage is the most profitable
The report is broken
Deals skip that stage entirely
questions.explain: An unusually long average time in one stage is the signal to investigate why deals wait there. Also confirm history tracking has been on long enough.
